cues.en: Lecturer: Welcome to this section of the course on clustering and dimension reduction.
cues.zh: 講師：歡迎來到分群與降維單元。

cues.en: These are techniques that kind of fit more into the traditional machine learning umbrella than the statistics umbrella.
cues.zh: 這些技術比較屬於傳統機器學習，而非統計學。

cues.en: So we're gonna start with k-means clustering, which is a simple but powerful method for clustering data.
cues.zh: 先介紹 K-means 分群，簡單但強大。

cues.en: It sometimes works really, really, amazingly well.
cues.zh: 有時效果驚人地好。

cues.en: It's a beautiful algorithm, but it can be pretty tricky to apply in a lot of real world applications where the clustering is a little bit difficult
cues.zh: 是漂亮的演算法，但實際應用中，若群集難以

cues.en: to see by eye.
cues.zh: 目視辨識，可能很難套用。

cues.en: Okay, so let's get started.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: So the goal of k-means clustering is to group multidimensional data into K groups.
cues.zh: K-means 的目標，是把多維資料分成 K 組。

cues.en: That's where this K comes from.
cues.zh: K 就是這個意思。

cues.en: K-means is the number of clusters.
cues.zh: K-means 的 K 是群集數。

cues.en: And so we define group membership by distances.
cues.zh: 依距離定義群組歸屬。

cues.en: So we say that groups or members are part of a group if they are all close to each other, and groups are different from each other if they are far apart from each other.
cues.zh: 成員彼此接近，就屬於一組；群組彼此距離遠，就不同組。

cues.en: So that, you know, that's kind of a sensible approach.
cues.zh: 這是合理方式。

cues.en: So the goal of k-means clustering or the general way that it works, and I'll explain the algorithm in a few moments, but the general concept of k-means clustering is that,
cues.zh: K-means 分群的目標，或說它大致的運作方式；稍後會解釋演算法，但一般概念是，

cues.en: it tries to minimize the distances within a group and maximize the distances between different groups.
cues.zh: 盡量縮小組內距離，並增大不同群組間距離。

cues.en: So that's the idea.
cues.zh: 概念如此。

cues.en: Okay, so here, I'm gonna show you an example and then we will walk through the algorithm.
cues.zh: 先看例子，再走過演算法。

cues.en: So here, this looks like a sort of cloud of data, but in fact, there are clusters in here.
cues.zh: 看起來是一團資料，但其實裡面有群集。

cues.en: So I tossed these data into k-means clustering algorithm with K = 3.
cues.zh: 把資料丟進 K 等於 3 的 K-means。

cues.en: So I told k-means to give me back three clusters, and here, we see the results, looks pretty compelling, you know.
cues.zh: 要求回傳三群，這是結果，相當有說服力。

cues.en: It's certainly a lot more clustered than the raw data.
cues.zh: 確實比原始資料看起來更像分成群了。

cues.en: Actually, when you see these clusters now, so these circles are the empirical centroids, and the lines, of course,
cues.zh: 這些圓圈是經驗質心，線條

cues.en: go from each dot to its own centroid.
cues.zh: 從各資料點連到所屬質心。

cues.en: So then, when you look at the raw data, now, you can actually see where these clusters are.
cues.zh: 再看原始資料，現在就看得出群集在哪。

cues.en: Now, I simulated these data so I know exactly where these clusters really should be, and that's the yellow stars that you see here.
cues.zh: 因為是模擬資料，所以我知道真正群集位置，就是黃色星星。

cues.en: So these are the centroids that I defined, and then I added clouds of noise around each of these centroids,
cues.zh: 是我定義的質心，再在各質心周圍加入一團雜訊，

cues.en: and then I subjected this to k-means with K = three.
cues.zh: 再以 K 等於 3 進行 K-means。

cues.en: And then the red circles here show the empirical means that were identified.
cues.zh: 紅圈是辨識出的經驗平均值。

cues.en: So quite close in all cases, a little bit pushed off over here, but that's okay.
cues.zh: 各處都很接近，這裡稍微偏移，但沒關係。

cues.en: There are actually many different k-means algorithms.
cues.zh: K-means 演算法其實有很多種。

cues.en: They get from quite basic to quite sophisticated, quite advanced, but all k-means algorithms basically follow the same formula.
cues.zh: 從基本到複雜、進階，但基本上遵循同一框架。

cues.en: And the more advanced algorithms like hierarchical k-means and Bayesian k-means, they're basically just taking the fundamental framework
cues.zh: 進階的階層 K-means、貝氏 K-means，基本上都是採用基礎架構，

cues.en: and expanding on it and trying to improve upon it.
cues.zh: 再擴充、嘗試改善。

cues.en: So what I'm gonna do now is walk you through this basic framework.
cues.zh: 現在走過基本架構。

cues.en: And once you understand that, then it's easy to get how these other k-means algorithm derivations are also working.
cues.zh: 理解後，就容易了解其他變體如何運作。

cues.en: Okay, so we start by selecting K.
cues.zh: 首先選 K。

cues.en: Now, this is not something that the algorithm does.
cues.zh: 不是演算法決定。

cues.en: This is something that you, the human being, does.
cues.zh: 是你這個人來決定。

cues.en: I assume you're a human being.
cues.zh: 假設你是人類。

cues.en: Now, I'm gonna talk more about selecting the right K in a few moments, and you'll also see how difficult this can be in the code
cues.zh: 稍後會多談選正確 K，下一支程式影片也會看到

cues.en: in the next video.
cues.zh: 這有多難。

cues.en: So once you've selected K, then the algorithm takes over, and it creates K centroids at totally random locations inside the dataset.
cues.zh: 選好 K，演算法接手，在資料集內完全隨機位置建立 K 個質心。

cues.en: So let's say we set K to be three.
cues.zh: 假設 K 為 3。

cues.en: So the algorithm is gonna start by selecting three random locations for the centroids, and it could happen that you get one centroid here, the second centroid over here,
cues.zh: 一開始選三個隨機位置，可能第一個在這裡、第二個在那裡，

cues.en: and the third centroid all the way down here.
cues.zh: 第三個在下面很遠的地方。

cues.en: That can happen.
cues.zh: 有可能如此。

cues.en: So there are, you know, other more advanced methods will guess good locations to come up with a good starting point for K, but essentially, they just start off at random locations.
cues.zh: 其他進階方法，會猜測比較好的起始位置，但基本上就是從隨機位置開始。

cues.en: Okay, then what you do is compute the sum of squared distances or errors from each data point to each of the K centroids, and this is computed as Euclidean distance,
cues.zh: 接著計算每個資料點到 K 個質心的平方距離和，或誤差，使用歐幾里得距離，

cues.en: which I've already shown you before in this course.
cues.zh: 這門課之前展示過。

cues.en: So let's say, you know, cluster centroid one is over here.
cues.zh: 假設第一個質心在這裡。

cues.en: So we compute the distance from this data point to the centroid, this data point to the centroid, all of the data points to each of the three centroids.
cues.zh: 計算這個點到質心、這個點到質心，全部資料點到三個質心各自的距離。

cues.en: So we get all of these distances.
cues.zh: 得到所有距離。

cues.en: Okay, and then what we do is we label each data point.
cues.zh: 接著標記每個資料點。

cues.en: So we categorize each data point according to the centroid that it's closest to.
cues.zh: 依最近的質心分類。

cues.en: So let's call this one, A, and this one, B, and this one, C.
cues.zh: 這個叫 A，這個 B，這個 C。

cues.en: So these data points are closest to A, maybe these ones are closer to B, and then a lot of these data points are gonna be closer to C.
cues.zh: 這些點最接近 A，也許這些較接近 B，很多其他點較接近 C。

cues.en: Okay, so each data point gets categorized or labeled according to its closest centroid.
cues.zh: 每個點都依最近質心分類、標記。

cues.en: And then step five is, once we've categorized that, then we take the average of all of the data points that were given a label of A,
cues.zh: 第五步，分類完成後，取所有標為 A 的資料點平均，

cues.en: and move A so that it's now at the center, the average of all of the A data points, and same thing with B.
cues.zh: 移動 A 到所有 A 點的中心、平均位置，B 同樣。

cues.en: So all of the data points that got labeled as being closest to B, the new location of B becomes the average of all of those data points, and same thing for C.
cues.zh: 所有最接近 B 的點，其平均值就成為 B 的新位置，C 同理。

cues.en: Okay, so that's step five, create new centroid at the average of all the data points that are labeled as being closest to that centroid.
cues.zh: 第五步，就是把質心移到所有被標為最接近它的點之平均。

cues.en: So you can see the data aren't moving around, of course.
cues.zh: 資料本身當然不動。

cues.en: It's just the centroid that gets pushed around at each step.
cues.zh: 只是每步推動質心。

cues.en: So that's basically how the fundamental algorithm works.
cues.zh: 基本演算法就是如此。

cues.en: Then the idea is we repeat steps three through five until we get to some measure of convergence.
cues.zh: 重複第三到第五步，直到滿足某種收斂指標。

cues.en: And basically, the measure of convergence is gonna be something about how much the mean is moving the centroid.
cues.zh: 基本上，收斂指標與質心移動多少有關。

cues.en: So when the centroids are not really in their proper place, then they're gonna keep bouncing around.
cues.zh: 質心還沒到適當位置，就會持續移動。

cues.en: They keep getting pulled around by their average of the data values that belong to that group.
cues.zh: 持續被屬於該群的資料平均值拉動。

cues.en: And then once the centroid is really in the middle of that group, you can see from iteration to iteration, the centroid isn't going to be moving around.
cues.zh: 真正到群組中央後，每次迭代就不再移動。

cues.en: Maybe it moves a tiny bit but the movements will be very, very small.
cues.zh: 也許稍微動一點，但非常非常小。

cues.en: So that's when we know to stop, and then we return all of the labels and the distances, and so on.
cues.zh: 這時就知道該停止，回傳標籤、距離等等。

cues.en: Okay, so sounds pretty cool, it sounds pretty straightforward, but there are some difficulties with k-means.
cues.zh: 聽起來很酷、直接，但 K-means 有些困難。

cues.en: So one thing is that it can be difficult to know a priori, the proper K, the proper number of means, of centroids, of groups.
cues.zh: 有時很難事先知道正確 K，也就是平均值、質心、群組數。

cues.en: Now, you know, you might think that there should be some simple algorithm that can loop through a bunch of different K parameters and tell us about what is the proper case.
cues.zh: 你可能以為有簡單演算法，對許多 K 迴圈，告訴我們正確值。

cues.en: It's a little bit like, you know, when there's section on regression, when I was talking about the polynomial regression, it needs the base information criteria, and so on.
cues.zh: 有點像迴歸章節中談多項式迴歸時，使用貝氏資訊準則等方法的情況。

cues.en: So the thing is, there are examples like that.
cues.zh: 其實確實有這類方法。

cues.en: There are methods, there's probably half a dozen different methods for determining the optimal number of clusters to extract.
cues.zh: 大概有五、六種方法，判定最佳群集數。

cues.en: But the thing is, those methods in like simple examples that you'll find on someone's data science blog, those methods work really well,
cues.zh: 資料科學部落格的簡單例子裡，這些方法效果很好，

cues.en: and you'll see some examples of that.
cues.zh: 你也會看到例子。

cues.en: But when you get to real data, it becomes really difficult.
cues.zh: 但真實資料就很難。

cues.en: First of all, it can be ambiguous.
cues.zh: 首先，可能模糊不清。

cues.en: Second of all, you will often see that trying out different methods for evaluating proper K will give you conflicting results.
cues.zh: 其次，不同 K 評估方法，經常給出互相矛盾的結果。

cues.en: So you might have one method, let's say, like the elbow method, and that tells you that three, a cluster size of three is optimal.
cues.zh: 例如肘部法認為三群最佳。

cues.en: And then a different method will tell you that a cluster size of five is optimal.
cues.zh: 另一種方法卻說五群最佳。

cues.en: So different quantitative methods will often give different results for the appropriate K in real world data.
cues.zh: 真實資料中，不同量化方法常給出不同 K。

cues.en: Another issue is that multidimensional clustering is difficult or impossible to visualize, and there are ways to sort of get around this.
cues.zh: 另一個問題，多維分群很難，甚至無法視覺化，也有一些迂迴方式。

cues.en: You can do a dimension reduction based on PCA, principle components analysis, which I'll talk about later on in this section.
cues.zh: 例如用 PCA 主成分分析降維，本單元稍後會談。

cues.en: But PCA is also not a magic bullet, and you know, it's still can be very difficult.
cues.zh: 但 PCA 也不是萬靈丹，仍可能非常難。

cues.en: You know, sort of mathematically, you can reduce the dimensionality to two or three, but that doesn't mean that it's a good dimension reduction that actually facilitates.
cues.zh: 數學上可降成二維或三維，不代表這是好的、有幫助的降維。

cues.en: It might actually just be making things more confusing.
cues.zh: 反而可能更混亂。

cues.en: Okay, another issue is that repeating the algorithm multiple times can give very different results.
cues.zh: 另外，演算法重複多次，可能得到很不一樣的結果。

cues.en: And you can imagine that's the case because we are just randomly placing these centroids around in the data space.
cues.zh: 可以想像，因為起始質心是隨機放在資料空間。

cues.en: So what number four means is that when you, you know, you have exactly the same data and you run exactly the same k-means clustering method
cues.zh: 第四點的意思是，完全相同資料、完全相同 K-means 方法，

cues.en: and you can get different results each time you run the same method because of the initial conditions are starting off as being random.
cues.zh: 每次結果可能不同，因為初始條件隨機。

cues.en: You can also have some problems when the cluster sizes differ.
cues.zh: 群集大小不同，也可能有問題。

cues.en: So let's say you have 10 data points in cluster one but 100 data points in cluster two.
cues.zh: 例如第一群 10 點，第二群 100 點。

cues.en: So k-means, it doesn't really deal with differences in cluster sizes very well.
cues.zh: K-means 不太擅長處理這種大小差異。

cues.en: And finally, you know, k-means is entirely based on the idea that group membership is defined by Euclidean distance in the data space.
cues.zh: 最後，它完全基於群組歸屬由資料空間中的歐幾里得距離定義。

cues.en: Now, that might be fine, but it's also possible that there are clusters, there are labelings, categories that are not defined purely by distance,
cues.zh: 這可能合理，但也可能有些群集、標籤、類別，並非純粹由距離，

cues.en: and maybe not by this Euclidean distance in the data space.
cues.zh: 或這種歐幾里得距離定義。

cues.en: So the assumptions underlying k-means clustering might not even be relevant in the data.
cues.zh: 因此 K-means 背後假設，甚至可能不適用。

cues.en: Okay, I don't mean to be so disparaging.
cues.zh: 我不是故意貶低它。

cues.en: K-means clustering is a really powerful and really great method, but it's important to realize that k-means clustering is always going to give you results.
cues.zh: K-means 非常強大、很好，但要知道它總會給出結果。

cues.en: I'll talk about this more with k-nearest neighbors as well.
cues.zh: 談 K 最近鄰時，也會多說。

cues.en: It's always going to give you some kind of a result, and it can be difficult to know whether that's the correct result or the optimal result.
cues.zh: 總有某種結果，但很難知道正確、最佳與否。

cues.en: So in practice, k-means clustering works well sometimes, and it really doesn't work well other times.
cues.zh: 實務上，有時效果好，有時很差。

cues.en: Okay, I'd like to give you a visual example to highlight how k-means works, and one of the difficulties, not just with k-means, but with clustering in general.
cues.zh: 舉視覺例子，凸顯它的運作與一個不只 K-means，而是一般分群的困難。

cues.en: So here, we have some data.
cues.zh: 有一些資料。

cues.en: It's like, you know, a sad face and a smiley face.
cues.zh: 像悲傷的臉與笑臉。

cues.en: And then there were two different clustering algorithms that were applied, k-means and this method called optics, which is pretty similar to k-nearest neighbor
cues.zh: 套用兩種演算法，K-means 與 OPTICS，後者有點類似

cues.en: that I will talk about in a few videos from now.
cues.zh: 幾支影片之後要談的 K 最近鄰。

cues.en: So you can see that they give different results, and the question is, you know, which one is right and which one is better, which one is wrong?
cues.zh: 結果不同，哪個對、哪個好、哪個錯？

cues.en: There's probably something, you know, you might have the intuition that this one is better.
cues.zh: 你可能直覺這個比較好。

cues.en: But why do you think that?
cues.zh: 但為什麼？

cues.en: You know, your brain's visual system has these, they're called Gestalt principles in psychology.
cues.zh: 大腦視覺系統有心理學所謂的完形原則。

cues.en: So there's these principles of sensory perception and understanding the world that are just based on some assumptions about the world.
cues.zh: 一些感官知覺、理解世界的原則，基於對世界的假設。

cues.en: So your brain's visual system works from the assumption that things that are close to each other belong together.
cues.zh: 視覺系統假設，彼此接近的東西屬於一起。

cues.en: So that's like a continuity principle, but we don't actually know whether that's really the case.
cues.zh: 類似連續性原則，但不知道實際是否如此。

cues.en: It could be that this is actually the correct clustering and this is incorrect.
cues.zh: 也許這才是正確分群，另一個錯。

cues.en: So for example, you know, imagine each one of these dots is a tree, and this is the property line.
cues.zh: 例如每點是一棵樹，這是土地界線。

cues.en: So this is my property, this is your property.
cues.zh: 這是我的地，這是你的。

cues.en: And, you know, let's say, you and I, we're not very good neighbors, we're not friendly, we don't like each other.
cues.zh: 假設我們是很差的鄰居，不友善、互相討厭。

cues.en: I don't want my trees on your property, you don't want your trees on my property.
cues.zh: 不想我的樹在你的地，也不想你的樹在我的地。

cues.en: So this is the dividing line.
cues.zh: 這是分界線。

cues.en: So then, this is actually the correct result, and this is the incorrect result because that means that, you know, I have to water your trees, and so on.
cues.zh: 那這才正確，另一個錯，因為會讓我得澆你的樹等等。

cues.en: Maybe that wasn't a good example.
cues.zh: 也許不是好例子。

cues.en: I'm sure if you and I were neighbors, we would get along really well, go out for beers every weekend, and so on.
cues.zh: 相信真的當鄰居，我們會相處很好，每週末一起喝啤酒等等。

cues.en: But the point is that, just because you get a result doesn't mean that it's necessarily the correct result.
cues.zh: 重點是，有結果不代表必然正確。

cues.en: You have to know more about the dataset to know whether you're getting a good result.
cues.zh: 必須更了解資料集，才知道結果是否好。

cues.en: And the second point here is that, different clustering methods are going to give you different results, and that's just how it is.
cues.zh: 第二，不同分群方法會得到不同結果，就是如此。

cues.en: It can be really challenging to know which is the right clustering method to apply because they're all based on different assumptions.
cues.zh: 因為基於不同假設，很難知道該用哪個。

cues.en: And without a really good understanding of the data and where the data come from and what the data mean, it can be really easy to apply the wrong clustering method
cues.zh: 不充分了解資料、來源與意義，很容易用錯分群方法，

cues.en: without realizing that you're getting suboptimal results.
cues.zh: 卻沒意識到結果並非最佳。

cues.en: All right, so in this video, I introduced you to k-means clustering, the basic algorithm of how k-means clustering works, and I talk quite a bit about k-means
cues.zh: 這支影片介紹 K-means 與基本演算法，也談了很多 K-means，

cues.en: but also just clustering in general, why it seems really great when you look at it on someone's blog, but in real applications, you have to take these clustering methods
cues.zh: 以及一般分群，為什麼部落格上看起來很棒，實際應用卻必須

cues.en: with a big grain of salt because they don't, they always produce results but it can be difficult to know whether you're really doing the right thing.
cues.zh: 審慎看待，因為它們總能產生結果，但很難知道做得是否正確。
